results.name: explain_safety_gmp
results.reply: The safety score of 7.4 (3rd percentile) is dragged down mainly by **violent and sexual offences at 88 per 1,000 residents** (score 4.1) and **serious road collisions nearby** (~9/year within 500 m, score 0.8). Two important caveats make this score less straightforward than it looks: the neighbourhood has only about 1,000 residents but sits in a busy city centre, so the rate denominator is tiny while the numerator still captures crimes affecting the many workers and visitors who pass through — and all crime figures here are **estimated**, because Greater Manchester Police doesn't publish street-level data. In other words, the score partly reflects the area's role as a commercial hub rather than the day-to-day risk for the small number of people who actually live there. If safety is a top priority, it's worth comparing against residential neighbourhoods on the edge of the city where the resident-to-visitor ratio is more balanced.

results.name: explain_high_score
results.reply: Hampstead (Camden 002C) sits at the 76th percentile, driven almost entirely by near-perfect **amenities** (99.6 — top-tier pubs, cafés, culture and a supermarket 260 m away), **schools** (97.1) and **transport** (95.0 — a station 147 m away plus gigabit broadband). The big drags are **safety** (19.2, where burglary, theft and anti-social behaviour all score single digits) and **affordability** (15.3, with a typical price of ~£1.39 m and a 20× price-to-income ratio). In short: an excellent place to live in almost every service and amenity sense, but expensive and not especially safe — the classic Hampstead trade-off.
